title: Fitness is a Pyramid Scheme and you're a minion
summary: Building on a blackpill article, NH argues that the fitness industry is a pyramid scheme. Supplement companies sit at the top, PED-using influencers in the middle, and natural lifters who buy products form the base. The scheme works by selling young men their own desire for muscle and masculinity. His answer is to stop consuming, because training knowledge is free and masculinity cannot be bought.
claims: The fitness industry is a pyramid: manufacturers on top, influencers in the middle, buyers (the minions) at the base
People fall for it through desire and lack of emotional control, not low intelligence
The US fitness industry makes about 30 billion dollars a year, yet lifting knowledge is free online
Influencers exist because people only buy from someone they feel parasocially connected to, not from a faceless corporation
Remember that influencers need you more than you need them
Consuming aspirational content does not move you toward the goal; it wastes time you could spend pursuing it
Supplements attach the image of a muscular body to the product, so buyers unconsciously expect to look like the seller
Knowing a marketing bias does not disarm the instinct; reason has to rein it in afterwards
Programs for sale are usually garbage because effort goes into marketing, not content; you can write your own
A testosterone booster sold by an enhanced 230 lb lifter sells far more than one sold by an ordinary person
The supplement industry was born with steroids in the 60s-70s; early Weider magazines already ran whey ads beside enhanced physiques
Without PEDs the fitness industry would never have existed, since naturals had only hard work to sell
Products are designed to keep novices small so they stay customers
People who realise the scam usually become blackpilled, hop to another influencer, or join the scheme by taking PEDs
The real crime of fake natties is killing trust, which pushes people to stop believing they can grow naturally
The 'might as well try it in case it works' mindset (as with turkesterone and ecdysterone) is what funds the industry
Fitness products sell masculinity, but real masculinity (dedication, pain tolerance, sacrifice) is internal and cannot be bought
The industry funded the biggest and freakiest bodybuilders and so killed natural bodybuilding
Buying a product is paying for the right to believe in yourself; only your actions build muscle
Influencers blame you when the product fails and take credit when you succeed
The Doucette and More Plates More Dates Blitz controversy was never about the supplement being bunk; buying a supplement to get big was the problem
The only way out is to stop playing: refuse to consume, since fitness is free and the hard work is yours
